text.p: SME - Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar said Slovakia's economic development could lead the country into the top ten of the world most developed countries by the year 2010.

- Meciar said the government had approved an unspecified development programme for the arms industry worth some five billion crowns. He said the government did not plan an increase in energy prices and rents for citizens before the general elections in 1998.

- The ultra-left junior coalition partner, the Workers Party (ZRS), plans to propose another amendment to a law on bank privatisation, barring the sell-off of the largest commercial banks VUB and IRB. ZRS leader Jan Luptak has said those ZRS deputies who helped the parliament allow privatisation of VUB and IRB voted for the law by mistake.

- If there are attempts to privatise the VUB and IRB before ZRS proposes a law barring the move, Stefan Gavornik, ZRS deputy chairman and the President of the National Property Fund - the agency in charge of the privatisation of state asstes - will not sign the sell-off and resign his post, Luptak said.

- Deputies of both the coalition and opposition parties will carry out an inspection of the ministry of culture, following allegations by striking actors of mismanagement of the cultural sector by Culture Minister Ivan Hudec.

NARODNA OBRODA -Premier Meciar said the current anti- government protests by actors, students and trade unions were part of the opposition strategy to change the political leadership in the country. Meciar said his Movement for a Democratic Slovakia (HZDS) would not surrender to such attempts and would protect democracy.

- Jan Gabriel, president of VUB, said his bank could complete restructuring of its loan protfolio within two years if it strengthens its capital resources and if legislation profits from classified assets tax exempt.

- Gabriel said a merger with the largest savings bank, Slovenska Sporitelna, was a way to increase competitiveness of the domestic banking sector, but that such a move cannot be carried out too quickly.

- A French-Slovak joint-venture producing polyamide wires, Chemlon Humenne, posted turnover of 4.3 billion crowns in 1996. Chemlon exported about 90 percent of its production last year, with more than half of the output going to EU markets. The company plans a development programme worth some 350 million crowns this year.
- ZRS said it was considering proposing an amendment to the banking law, permitting the Highest Control Bureau to carry out audits of banks.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Engineering soncern SES Tlmace has won an 800 million Czech crown contract to upgrade a heating utitlity in Praha-Malesice, Czech Republic.
